description:
We are currently a team of two, bringing together software development and an interest in using technology to solve real-world problems. We are developers with experience building web applications and APIs, while having a  collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for learning and problem-solving.

We have express strong interest in Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, and we hope to build a practical solution that helps farmers make better-informed decisions using NASA data.
summary: FieldShift helps farmers in Ghana choose crops that suit their land as rainfall and heat patterns shift. A farmer or extension officer picks a location, and FieldShift pulls a full year of daily temperature, rainfall and sunlight data from NASA POWER. It compares that climate profile with 12 reference locations across Ghana, assigns the farm one of 11 farming zones, and recommends crops that fit. This addresses the challenge by turning NASA climate data into a simple, practical decision for farmers who don't have agronomists or weather tools. It matters because a wrong crop choice can wipe out a season's income. FieldShift is free and needs no account.
details:
• What it does: It turns a location into a farming zone and a crop list, using real NASA climate data.
    • The React and Vite app sends the location to an Express and Node API.
    • The API fetches the previous calendar year of daily data from NASA POWER's agriculture data set, covering temperature (T2M), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR) and sunlight (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).
    • It averages those values and compares them with 12 reference locations in Ghana, using a nearest-neighbour method that looks at the 3 closest matches.
    • The result is a zone, a confidence score and recommended crops.
  • Benefits: Climate-aware crop choices for smallholder farmers, at no cost and with no sign-up.
  • Tools: React, Vite, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, Render and Vercel.
  • Next steps: Planting-window hints from the same daily data, and tools for agricultural extension officers.
